author: Tushar Singh
purpose: Out-of-sample test of the claims made on the first 15 tasks, on 15 new tasks in 3 new occupations, with the same instruments; plus the 4 previously skipped tasks; plus repeats.

dataset.name: openai/gdpval
dataset.selection_rule: scripts/select_slice_v31.py: keep the original 3 occupations; add every other occupation whose 5 gold deliverables are all native .docx/.xlsx (2 qualify); fill to 30 from the 4/5 tier, ties broken by sharing a sector with the original slice (1 qualifies). Applied mechanically; see data/gdpval_v31/selection_report.json.

new: First-Line Supervisors of Production and Operating Workers

tiers.A: native docx/xlsx deliverable, references from the dataset; unchanged from v3
tiers.P: PowerPoint deliverable; solver told python-pptx is available; extractor reads slide text
tiers.W: task requires public web research; solver may use its own web tools and must cite URL and retrieval date; no pinned source, so the judge can check internal consistency and cited figures only; reported separately
tiers.D: PDF deliverable; extractor reads page text

tasks.adaptation: live web research permitted; v3 skipped it for lack of a pinned snapshot
live web research permitted; v3 skipped it for lack of a pinned snapshot

instances.repeats: r1 for every instance; r2 for every instance after r1, judging and labels

instruments_unchanged.solvers: Claude Code CLI headless, models sonnet and opus (Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5), same flags; per-episode timeout 3600 s
instruments_unchanged.solver_preamble: identical to v3 for tier A; tiers P, W and D append one sentence each (format library; web permission and citation duty; PDF writer)
instruments_unchanged.requirement_selection: CAP=10, heuristic-critical first then operative-keyword rank, unchanged
instruments_unchanged.judge_settings: max_tokens 12000, reasoning medium, json_object, no provider fallbacks, unchanged
instruments_unchanged.packet_change: reference text capped at 240,000 characters per packet in total (no v3 packet exceeded it); pptx and pdf deliverables extracted as text
instruments_unchanged.validator_change: quote locators for ppt/ and pdf: units are stripped like xl/ and word/ locators; nothing else changes

population_and_sets.R_replication: the 15 tasks in the 3 new occupations x 2 solvers, r1 (30 outputs): out-of-sample for every claim below
population_and_sets.S_previously_skipped: 02aa1805, 5349dd7b (tier W), 3c19c6d1, 552b7dd0 (tier P) x 2 solvers, r1: reported separately
population_and_sets.F_full: all 30 tasks x 2 solvers, r1 (60 outputs), plus 3 conflict variants x 2

random_sample.population: all F_full original-variant r1 outputs not already human-labeled
random_sample.design: stratified by occupation, round-robin over the 6 occupations, Sonnet/Opus alternating, seed 20261106
random_sample.frozen: immediately after solve r1 completes and before any v3.1 judge result is opened
random_sample.blinding: packets contain request, sources and full output text only; labels written before any judge text is seen

confound_check.set: every historical GPT-6.1 Sol r1 output in the two families where Claude errors were confirmed (sourcing_approvals, supplier_exit) not already reviewed: 5 outputs
confound_check.purpose: tests whether the 11-to-0 behaviour-failure split reflects the Sol judge or the solver

endpoints: consequential_error (with quoted output and source lines)
human_review.second_reviewer: kit provided; κ reported if a second reviewer labels the same packets; otherwise stated as a limit

predictions.claim: The failure class replicates out of sample: at least one human-confirmed consequential error in R sits in an operative section (action table, schedule, exception or provisional clause, workbook total or formula) of a deliverable that states the governing rule or figure correctly elsewhere.
predictions.fails_if: no such case among the labeled R outputs

predictions.claim: Judge strictness ordering holds: on R, outputs with any honored failure under Gemini but none under Sol number at most 2.

Preference and rubric disagree: in at least one R pair where a judge's rubric max severity differs between the two solvers, that judge's preference verdict (position-consistent) goes to the higher-severity output.
predictions.fails_if: no such pair for either judge

predictions.claim: Gemini is more lenient than Sol on real errors: among human-confirmed consequential errors in the random sample, Gemini passes at least as many as Sol.
predictions.fails_if: Sol passes more confirmed errors than Gemini

predictions.claim: Preference judges reproduce the leaderboard order: both prefer Opus in a majority of position-consistent R pairs. Reported as what preference measures, not as quality.
predictions.fails_if: either judge prefers Opus in half or fewer

estimates_reported: consequential-error prevalence on the random sample with a Wilson 95% interval
per-judge sensitivity and specificity against human labels with counts
per-judge stated-but-not-honored counts on R and F
r1-vs-r2 agreement per instance per judge
all of the above by occupation and solver, as counts

budget_usd_cumulative_guards.note: judge ledgers are cumulative over the study; v3 already spent 17.43 on judging

stop_rules: no change to judge prompt, rubric selection, or solver preamble for tier A after any v3.1 output exists
transport failure above 20% after retries: stop and fix transport
the random sample is frozen before any v3.1 judge result is opened
every outcome is reported, including predictions that fail
